frames.label: 1m-context-retrieval-chart
frames.transcript_anchor: 1:11–1:20 "You can see right around that 250k mark is where things start degrading. But how fast things degrade really matters."
frames.why_for_weak_student: The single technical exhibit for innovation #1: the MRCR v2 8-needle 'Long context retrieval' chart (Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro across 128K→1M). Shows the Claude 4.6 lines staying high across the full window while others fall off — the visual proof of 'true 1M context'.
frames.caveat: Carries a small burned-in caption ('right around that') and a highlight ring on 256K from the video; the chart itself is fully legible.

frames.label: boot-roster-models-1m
frames.transcript_anchor: 9:34–9:49 "If I type J, which is an alias for just... J CEO... we're presented with our CEO and board, our strategic decision-making multi-agent team."
frames.why_for_weak_student: What 'success at step zero' looks like: the boot screen after `j ceo` shows the launch command, Time 2–5 min / Budget $1–$5 / Editor code, and the full roster with models — CEO [anthropic/claude-opus-4-6 1M] and every board member [anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 1M]. Confirms 'Opus on the CEO, Sonnet on the board' and the 1M badge.

frames.label: ceo-board-architecture-diagram
frames.transcript_anchor: 3:29–3:44 & 27:50 "You sit at the top, you have a customized agent harness, and then we have a multi-agent orchestration pattern... a single node going out to multiple agents."
frames.why_for_weak_student: THE system diagram: You, the Engineer → Pi Extension → CEO (Opus 4.6) → converse() lines → all 8 board members (Revenue, Product Strategist, Technical Architect, Contrarian, Compounder, Customer Oracle, Market Strategist, Moonshot). The one picture that makes multi-agent orchestration concrete.
frames.caveat: Composited over the overhead desk B-roll (semi-transparent), so slightly darker than a full-bleed slide — still fully legible. Clean SVG source available at images/main/05-ceo-board-architecture.svg if the chapter prefers.

frames.label: config-yaml-constraints
frames.transcript_anchor: 16:26–16:52 "Configuration file has a few key nodes. We have our meeting, which sets up all the constraints... brief sections... paths... customizable board members."
frames.why_for_weak_student: The control file, ceo-and-board-configuration.yaml: meeting.constraints (min_time 2, max_time 5, min_budget $1, max_budget $5), editor 'code', plus the collapsed brief_sections / paths / board nodes. Shows that the whole system is steered from one small, readable YAML.

frames.label: ceo-agent-frontmatter
frames.transcript_anchor: 18:36–19:07 "This looks very different from system prompts you're probably used to... Our CEO has expertise, it has skills, and of course it's got a model."
frames.why_for_weak_student: The customized agent front matter (ceo.md): name, expertise (ceo-scratch-pad.md, updatable:true), skills (svg-generate + tts-eleven with use-when), model anthropic/claude-opus-4-6, domain. Demystifies 'specialized system prompt with parsed front matter' completely.

frames.label: moonshot-personality-prompt
frames.transcript_anchor: 31:39–31:53 "The moonshot agent is our big bet thinker. And I love this line: What if we're thinking too small? You advocate for 10x moves, category-defining bets."
frames.why_for_weak_student: A board member's actual personality prompt (moonshot.md): Purpose ('Expand the aperture of possibility, challenge incrementalism') + Variables (CORE_BIAS Asymmetric upside, RISK_TOLERANCE Very High, DEFAULT_STANCE 'avoid cowardly incrementalism'). Shows how a controlled bias is engineered into an agent.

frames.label: brief-and-brief-library
frames.transcript_anchor: 20:28–21:52 "What does an actual brief look like?... Should we take the $12 million acquisition offer... We have stakes, constraints, and we have the key question."
frames.why_for_weak_student: The input side, made concrete: the acquisition-offer brief.md (Situation/Stakes/Constraints/Key Question) open next to the briefs/ file tree showing the whole library of example decisions. Shows both the required structure AND that briefs stack into a reusable corpus.

frames.label: parallel-deliberation-vote-tally
frames.transcript_anchor: 11:58–12:24 "This, of course, runs in parallel. This isn't sequential... they're all forming their own opinions... the room is four to one."
frames.why_for_weak_student: The deliberation in motion: converse('all') at the top ('Good round. The room is 4-to-1 leaning accept with Moonshot as the clear dissent'), all board members 'responding...' at once (parallel), TIME/BUDGET gauges (3.2 min / $1.37), and per-member cost in the footer. Shows parallelism + the adversarial vote + live constraints in one frame.

frames.label: constraint-max-reached
frames.transcript_anchor: 14:59–15:08 "Okay, max reached. So we are over in time. The CEO is going to end the deliberation... final position, one statement each."
frames.why_for_weak_student: The constraint engine doing its job: '6 response(s) | 7.2min | $3.39 [MAX REACHED]', the TIME bar pinned full. This is the moment the harness forces the meeting to wrap — the tangible payoff of 'real constraints on a meeting'.

frames.label: conversation-jsonl-observability
frames.transcript_anchor: 23:35–24:12 "Most importantly is the conversation. Observability is a key element of building powerful agentic systems... we have the from and the to."
frames.why_for_weak_student: The observability artifact: conversation.jsonl (meeting_start, then from/to/message for CEO/Revenue/Technical Architect/Moonshot 'Position: REJECT'/Contrarian/..., meeting_end) beside the deliberations/ tree full of generated SVGs (moonshot-value-trajectory.svg, revenue-exit-scenario-matrix.svg, contrarian-assumption-risk-map.svg…) and tool-use.jsonl. Proves the whole debate is logged and replayable.

frames.label: memo-output-decision-map
frames.transcript_anchor: 7:46–8:10 "You can see our CEO agent put together a decision map... top three recommendations here, fix the retention engine, then YouTube shorts."
frames.why_for_weak_student: The output side: the shorts-platform memo open in VS Code — title 'Which Shorts Platform Should We Lead With?', Decision Status DECIDED, the Final Decision paragraph, and the Decision Map (TikTok / Multi-plat / ✓YouTube Shorts / IG Reels / Kill Blog). Shows exactly what 'decision out' looks like.

frames.label: tts-audio-summary-skill
frames.transcript_anchor: 17:14–17:42 "The board recommends accepting NutraHoldings $12 million acquisition offer at 11 times ARR. The vote was five to one... that silence was the signal."
frames.why_for_weak_student: Closing the loop: the CEO invoking the tts-eleven skill (text_to_file.py … && afplay) to speak the memo — 'Synthesizing (569 chars)…', summary.mp3 saved, CEO [complete], TIME 11.6 min / BUDGET $4.61. Shows a skill turning a written memo into a spoken decision — customization on top of the base agent.
